title: Dynamic affinity allocator and decode-wave prefetch for tiled-KV paged-attention
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Paged-attention with tiled KV shards exhibits fragmentation across GPU memory slices and suboptimal kernel selection during rapid prefill/decode waves. This causes higher p50/p99 decode latency and excess memory churn under bursty conversational workloads.

Goal:
Design and implement a Dynamic Affinity Allocator (DAA) that groups logically adjacent KV tiles by reuse-distance and affinity, combined with a Decode-Wave Prefetch (DWP) scheduler that issues background prefill/transfer windows timed to decode waves. The system should: reduce allocation-induced fragmentation, improve kernel locality for tiled attention kernels, and limit stall time for decode hotpaths. Target outcomes: 8-15% p99 latency reduction on conversational traces, 10-20% reduction in token-level GPU memory churn, and a 12-18% effective cost reduction for typical multi-turn workloads.

Design overview:
- Affinity grouping heuristics: maintain a lightweight reuse-distance histogram per request type (chat/system/prompt) and assign incoming KV pages to affinity buckets (hot-warm-cold). Buckets prefer contiguous slab regions to reduce external fragmentation.
- Dynamic slot coalescing: when multiple small KV allocations are predicted to be used together (same affinity bucket, short reuse-distance), coalesce into a tiled super-slot that optimizes GPU kernel load patterns for tiled-attention kernels.
- Decode-Wave Prefetch (DWP): a scheduler that observes decode-rate signals (tokens/s, queue depth, tail-latency trend) and pre-issues DMA/page transfers in waves aligned to upcoming decode bursts, using conservative backpressure to preserve latency SLOs.
- Kernel selection hints: expose an internal hint from the allocator indicating expected contiguous tile layout and average sequence span; the kernel selector will prefer tiled-attention kernels and optimized memcpy paths when these hints indicate high locality.
- Background compaction: low-priority compaction pass that consolidates cold buckets during underutilized GPU windows; compaction uses incremental copy-and-free with rate limiting to avoid interfering with foreground decode.
- Eviction policy: replace LRU/LRUD with affinity-weighted reuse policy that biases evictions away from coalesced super-slots unless reuse-distance shows minimal probability. Eviction triggers integrate with DWP to prefetch warmed slots if a recently-evicted slot is requested.

Trade-offs considered:
- Coalescing increases worst-case reclaim cost (larger contiguous free required) but improves kernel throughput; mitigated via hybrid slicing of super-slots and fast split paths.
- DWP can increase background bandwidth usage; we limit to a percentage of available DMA and integrate with autoscaling signals to avoid SLO regressions.
- Complexity vs determinism: heuristics tuned for common chat workloads; fallbacks to conservative allocator for unknown workloads or when telemetry confidence is low.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype allocator module with affinity buckets and coalescing in a feature-flagged path. Add telemetry for reuse-distance, fragmentation ratio, and coalesced-slot hit-rate.
2) Implement DWP scheduler that subscribes to existing request rate telemetry and exposes knobs (window size, prefetch lookahead, bandwidth cap).
3) Extend kernel selector to accept allocator hints via the internal request descriptor. Bench tiled vs generic kernels on representative models (Llama2-70B, MPT-30B) and sequences.
4) Add background compaction and safe split/merge operations with unit/integration tests.
5) End-to-end integration tests on canary pool, followed by phased rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on metrics regressions.

Monitoring and acceptance signals:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 decode and prefill latency per-model and per-route.
- Resource: fragmentation ratio, free slab run-length distribution, coalesced-slot hit-rate, DMA bandwidth used by DWP.
- Correctness: zero increase in token corruption or KV-mismatch errors, verified by fuzz tests and golden prompt sets.
- Cost proxy: tokens/sec per GPU and estimated $/token.

Acceptance criteria:
- P99 decode latency reduced by >=8% on the internal multi-turn conversational trace set (compare baseline runtime-1.20).
- Fragmentation ratio decreased by >=10% and coalesced-slot hit-rate >=60% on live canary traffic.
- No increase in end-to-end error rate or correctness failures in integration tests.
- Feature gated and reversible with rollout flag and automated SLO-driven rollback.

Tasks:
- Implement DAA allocators with affinity bucket metadata and coalescing (ENG).
- Add telemetry and dashboard (Console/Observability).
- Implement DWP scheduler and integrate DMA controller knobs (ENG).
- Extend kernel selector to consume allocator hints (Runtime/Kernels team).
- Unit/integration tests for split/merge and compaction logic (QA/ENG).
- Benchmarking harness: run tiled vs generic kernels across batch/seq distributions (Bench).
- Canary rollout plan and postmortem runbook (SRE/Eng).

Links and artifacts:
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7321
- Benchmark notebooks and traces: https://internal.redwood.com/benchmarks/paged-kv/daawave-2026
- RisK s and mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive coalescing could cause rare OOMs on highly fragmented patterns. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, OOM backoff that disables coalescing per host, and canary with synthetic worst-case workloads.
- Risk: DWP could contend with other DMA traffic (model load). Mitigation: bandwidth caps and priority queues that yield to urgent transfers.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged dev builds -> bench cluster (2 weeks) -> canary pool (10% of traffic, 1 week) -> expand to 50% with gated metrics -> full rollout. Automated rollback triggers on p99 regression >5% or fragmentation increase >10%.
